title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Ignore the reason for the visit. Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for heart failure.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 96% on RA, Temp 98.6F, Weight 165 lbs.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, fatigue.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath, cough.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain, palpitations.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea, abdominal pain.
Neurological: Negative for dizziness, syncope.

HPI: Patient is a 77-year-old woman with a history of chronic systolic heart failure (HFrEF). She presents today for a scheduled follow-up to evaluate symptoms and medication efficacy. Patient reports she has been feeling well since the last visit. She denies any recent increase in peripheral edema or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. She reports adherence to her current diuretic and beta-blocker regimen.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Carvedilol 12.5mg twice daily
- Furosemide 40mg daily

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Regular rhythm, S1 and S2 heard, no murmurs, gallops, or rubs.
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: No trace of pitting edema, no cyanosis.

Assessment:
1. Chronic systolic heart failure (HFrEF): Patient is currently stable. Symptoms were reviewed and she denies significant fluid overload.

Plan:
1. Chronic systolic heart failure: Continue current medication regimen. Will monitor weight and symptoms at next visit.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, PA-C
October 14, 2026
explanations: The provider addressed chronic systolic heart failure at this visit, so it is supported: I50.22.

distractors.why: Status plus a plan in the assessment supports the diagnosis.
